title: CULTURING i3NEURONS (Basic Protocol 6)
author: Michael S. Fernandopulle
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.5jpg4mn
materials: Prepare stock solutions of PLO or PEI (see Table 3 ).

steps.title: Apply primary coating solution
steps.instruction: Add one half culture volume of the coating solution prepared in step 1 to each tissue‑culture dish that will receive Day 3 partially differentiated i³ Neurons. Gently tilt the plate to ensure full coverage.

steps.title: Incubate coated dishes
steps.instruction: Incubate the coated dishes for at least 1 hour at room temperature. For best results, incubate overnight in a 37 °C incubator.

steps.title: Wash and rinse dishes
steps.instruction: Rinse each dish with sterile water. Repeat the wash two more times for a total of three washes (four or more washes are recommended for PEI‑coated plates).

steps.title: Dry dishes completely
steps.instruction: Allow the washed dishes to dry completely in a biosafety cabinet (typically 30 min to 1 h). To accelerate drying, stand dishes on their sides and lean them against the back of the cabinet; lids may be left askew. If dishes are not used immediately, wrap them in aluminum foil and store at 4 °C for up to 1 week. Complete drying is essential for PEI‑coated plates to prevent toxicity.

steps.title: Optional laminin secondary coating
steps.instruction: For PLO (optional) or PEI (highly recommended) plates, perform a secondary coating with laminin: thaw concentrated laminin stock (~1 mg ml⁻¹) slowly on ice and dispense with chilled pipettes; dilute the stock to 10 µg ml⁻¹ in cold PBS; add one half culture volume of this laminin solution to the polymer‑coated, washed, and dried dishes; incubate for at least 2 hours at 37 °C; then aspirate the laminin solution before plating neurons.

steps.title: Prepare culture medium
steps.instruction: In a sterile biosafety cabinet, prepare the culture medium (CM). Optionally add doxycycline to a final concentration of 2 µg ml⁻¹. Choose a basal medium (e.g., BrainPhys, DMEM/F12, Neurobasal A) and supplement with B27, BDNF, NT‑3, and laminin as appropriate. BrainPhys is preferred for synapse formation and spontaneous activity, but other formulations may be used.

steps.title: Warm culture medium
steps.instruction: Place the prepared CM in a 37 °C water or bead bath for approximately 20 minutes, or until the medium feels warm to the touch.

steps.title: Resuspend and plate cells
steps.instruction: Thaw a cryovial of 3‑day differentiated i³ Neurons (or use freshly dissociated cells) and resuspend in the appropriate volume of medium. Plate according to the vessel:

substeps.instruction: 96‑well plate (imaging): 1–5 × 10⁴ cells in 100 µl medium per well.
8‑well chamber slide (imaging): 0.3–1.5 × 10⁵ cells in 250 µl medium per well.
6‑well plate (biochemistry): 1.5–2 × 10⁶ cells in 1.5 ml medium per well (supplement to 2–3 ml one day after plating).
10‑cm dish (biochemistry): 1–1.2 × 10⁷ cells in 8 ml medium (supplement to 10–12 ml one day after plating).
15‑cm dish (biochemistry): 3–3.5 × 10⁷ cells in 18 ml medium (supplement to 20–22 ml one day after plating).
For biochemistry plates, the initial volumes listed should be used; the next‑day supplement brings the cultures to the final volumes indicated.

steps.title: Optional astrocyte supplementation
steps.instruction: To improve long‑term health, add astrocytes or astrocyte‑conditioned medium (ACM):

substeps.instruction: Use primary astrocytes expanded in DMEM + 10 % FBS from post‑natal (P0‑3) mice or rats, low passage (< p3).
Astrocytes may be frozen in aliquots and thawed immediately before co‑culture at day 3.
If co‑culturing directly, use a ratio of 2 neurons : 1 astrocyte.
Alternatively, replace regular half‑medium changes with half‑medium changes of sterile‑filtered ACM.

steps.title: Monitor cultures daily
steps.instruction: Examine cultures daily under a phase‑contrast microscope. If high debris or clumping is observed, remove half the culture medium and replace it with a full volume of fresh medium (i.e., a 50 % increase). If debris persists, suspect insufficient coating or expired coating solution.

steps.title: Perform half‑medium changes
steps.instruction: Change half of the medium according to culture density:

substeps.instruction: Dense (biochemistry) cultures: replace half‑medium every 3–4 days (biweekly).
Aspirate slowly with a serological or micropipette, tilting the dish so medium pools on one side; dispense fresh medium toward the wall, away from cells.

Never dispense directly onto cells; if a full aspiration is required (e.g., PBS wash), add medium dropwise in the centre of the tilted well until a small pool forms in a corner, then add the remaining volume down the wall onto this pool to minimise shear forces.
